summary: Printed apparatus is welded onto the front of four released arcika verses by the parser.
detail: Leading editorial matter that belongs to the page apparatus, not the verse, is included in text_original. Every codepoint still comes from the pinned page, so this is not a codepoint-reproduction failure; it is a unit-boundary failure. The release containment check cannot see it because it collapses whitespace before comparing, which is what hides the join.
found_by: independent re-verification of the Samaveda codepoint gate

closure.not_applied_because: The agent staging this correction may not write to Neo4j and may not edit data/canonical in place. The proposal carries the exact Cypher and the exact corrected strings; applying it is a lead action.
closure.unit_count_independently_confirmed: A scan of every VG:WORK:SV:KAU TextVersion in the live graph for parentheses, brackets, asterisk, dagger, Latin letters, ASCII digits, 'cf.' and the cross-reference marker returned exactly these 4 and no others.
closure.evidence: In each case the apparatus stands on its own wikitext line AFTER the preceding verse's number marker and is separated from this verse by a blank line: it is the saman-name / cross-reference annotation of the PRECEDING verse. All four corrected readings occur verbatim in the pinned page in its line form, so the ORIGINAL text policy holds -- the unit narrows, no reading changes. SV CHANDA 2.7.7 is confirmed a second way: its corrected text hashes identically to the already-clean uttararcika duplicate VG:SV:KAU:UTTARA:P01:R02:D07:V01 (WS UTTARA.P1.R2.D7 RN731).
closure.downstream_after_apply: content_sha256 changes for all four, so referent_bindings text_sha256 must follow, the release manifest must be regenerated, and the derived USES_FORMULA / SHARES_FORMULA_WITH / REUSES_TEXT_FROM / NEAR_PARALLEL_OF edges for these four passages were computed over the apparatus and should be rebuilt.

summary: The canonical release under data/canonical/** is gitignored, so no released corpus is protected by git history.
detail: This is the same class of hazard already recorded for the sealed schema, which was once destroyed by a schema export and recovered only from a dangling git blob. It applies to every Veda, not only the Samaveda.
found_by: independent re-verification of the Samaveda codepoint gate

closure.resolution: The corpus stays gitignored -- 103.7 MB across the four projected releases, and the Rigvedic primary layer is CC BY-NC-SA, which data/builds/four_veda_corpus_candidate_manifest.json forbids republishing as one merged adapted work. What is now protected is the release's *identity*: a tracked per-file sha256 manifest, each build's own manifest.json un-ignored, and a verified external copy.
closure.gitignore_change: .gitignore now re-includes data/canonical/*/manifest.json (20 files, 875,702 bytes of per-file digests and record counts, no verse text). The corpus itself remains excluded.

external_snapshot.contents: the 62 RELEASE-tier files, plus SHA256 and MANIFEST.json
external_snapshot.verified: re-hashed at the destination: 62/62 matched, 0 missing, 0 mismatched
external_snapshot.caveat: Same physical volume as the repository (D:). It protects against a bad rebuild, a truncation or a stray export -- not against losing the drive. Off-volume replication is not claimed.

closure.prior_protection_measured: Each release already carried its own manifest.json with per-file sha256, but inside data/canonical/ and therefore gitignored: destroyed by the same event it would have detected. The two tracked semantic freezes in docs/manifests/ hash 71 and 67 files, of which 15 are canonical -- all rigveda_full_v1. The Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda releases had no tracked digest at all.
